title: From Oumuamua to Borisov & 3I/ATLAS: 3 Interstellar Objects To Ever Enter The Solar System
excerpt: There Was Something Unusual About Them. Find Out What.
content:
There Was Something Unusual About Them. Find Out What. 

By Mashable News Staff

24 September 2026

1I/Oumuamua

Discovered in October 2017 by astronomer Robert Weryk via Hawaii's Pan-STARRS 1 observatory, the cigar-shaped, asteroid-like object measured roughly 400-1000 meters long and displayed unexplained non-gravitational acceleration.

I/Oumuamua

Some speculated Oumuamua was an alien spy probe, but SETI's radio telescopes picked up no unusual emissions from it.

2I/Borisov

Discovered in August 2019 by amateur astronomer Gennady Borisov at his personal MARGO observatory in Nauchnij, Crimea, the roughly 1-kilometer-wide object became the first interstellar comet ever spotted.

2I/Borisov

Borisov made its closest approach to Earth on December 28, 2019, trailing a tail 14 times Earth's size, and even prompted proposals for an interception mission.

3I/Atlas

Discovered July 1, 2026, by the ATLAS observatory in Chile, the nearly 15-kilometer-wide interstellar comet. The interstellar interloper drew early doubts about its cometary nature and speculation it could be an alien probe. Scientists estimate 3I/Altas age to be older than the solar system itself. 

3I/Atlas

Harvard astrophysicist Prof. Avi Loeb identified at least 22 anomalies in the object, including an unusual composition and a nickel-rich gas plume typically associated with industrial production.

4I/Rubin Next Interstellar Object


Prof Avi Loeb has proposed NASA intercept the next interstellar object, dubbed 4I/Rubin, as soon as it's discovered, though the agency has said such a mission would need at least five years to prep.
